grade.rationale: The implementation is substantial and readable, but several core heuristics violate the sensor's stated conservative contract. Authentication and authorization can be overstated, security findings can consequently be suppressed, and detected boundaries can be silently discarded. Source-discovery failures and repository-containment gaps further undermine inventory completeness and trustworthiness.

summary: The sensor compiles according to the supplied analyzer evidence and has deterministic ordering, stable serialization, cancellation during file reads, and generally clear data models. Its main weakness is unsound inference: repository-wide or file-wide string matches are treated as endpoint-specific proof, authorization checks omit authenticated-but-unauthorized boundaries, and several parsing shortcuts can either suppress real findings or manufacture incorrect facts. No test coverage evidence was supplied, so coverage remains unknown.

grade.rationale: Authentication, authorization, origin validation, parameter binding, and controller-body attribution can all be reported incorrectly. These errors include security-relevant false negatives and contradict the documented unknown-until-proved policy.

The code is organized into named analysis passes, but large collections of loosely scoped regular expressions and file-wide substring joins create hidden coupling and make new language constructs likely to change unrelated results.

Names and record types communicate the intended inventory well, but values such as authenticated, required, repository-scoped, and origin-checked imply stronger guarantees than the associated evidence establishes.

Unreadable files disappear without diagnostics or an incomplete-inventory marker, while directory enumeration errors are not handled consistently. Callers can therefore receive either a deceptively complete result or an abrupt scan failure.

Most parsing and filesystem behavior is hardwired into private static methods, making focused substitution of source discovery and inference policies difficult. Coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was provided.

findings.title: Authentication middleware is treated as an endpoint requirement
findings.description: For every /api route in a file, the presence of StartsWithSegments("/api") and either Authenticate(context) or UseAuthentication() anywhere in that file upgrades the route to authenticated. UseAuthentication only populates the principal; it does not reject anonymous callers, and the substring checks do not establish control flow, ordering, or applicability to this endpoint. DeriveAuthorization similarly promotes every matching API route to repository-scoped when a recognized CanAccess call appears anywhere in the file. This can suppress the sensor's most important security findings despite the class contract promising that unproved facts remain unknown.
findings.recommendation: Build endpoint-specific evidence from syntax or semantic analysis. Treat authentication middleware as infrastructure only, require an endpoint authorization policy or a proven rejecting middleware branch, and associate repository-access checks with the actual handler control flow before upgrading either fact.

findings.title: Missing-authorization finding only examines authentication
findings.description: The rule titled "Inbound boundary has no derived authorization" tests Authentication.Value but never Authorization.Value. A boundary classified as authenticated with authorization none, unknown, or authenticated-only produces no missing-authorization finding. This is especially damaging because earlier broad heuristics readily upgrade authentication.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate authentication and authorization independently. Emit an authentication finding when credentials are not required and an authorization finding whenever Authorization.Value is none, unknown, or otherwise below the policy required for the boundary.

findings.title: Explicit ASP.NET parameter binding attributes are discarded
findings.description: ParseDotNetInputs removes all attributes from parameter before checking for FromHeader, FromBody, or FromRoute. Those checks can therefore never succeed. Parameters are instead classified using route-name and type heuristics, producing incorrect boundary input sources and potentially misleading downstream sink findings.
findings.recommendation: Extract binding metadata before removing attributes, or parse the parameter with Roslyn. Preserve attribute arguments as well, since attributes can rename the externally visible parameter.

findings.title: ID-based deduplication silently drops distinct boundaries
findings.description: Entries are deduplicated by StableId before mechanical checks. HTTP IDs contain only method and normalized route, so identical routes in different applications, files, frameworks, host groups, or duplicated registrations collapse into one entry. The retained entry's authentication, limits, side effects, and location depend on analyzer insertion order, and findings associated with discarded registrations are never evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Include application identity and source location in registration IDs, or merge duplicate registrations conservatively by retaining every location and selecting the least-protective fact. Run checks before any presentation-only grouping.

findings.title: Unreadable sources disappear without marking the inventory incomplete
findings.description: IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, and DecoderFallbackException are swallowed without recording a finding or completeness state. Contrary to the comment, facts from an unreadable file do not remain unknown; the file and all boundaries it may contain are absent. Consumers cannot distinguish a complete inventory from a partial scan.
findings.recommendation: Record a structured scan diagnostic for every skipped file and expose an incomplete status in the result or inventory. Include the path and failure category without leaking sensitive exception details, and let policy decide whether persistence is allowed for incomplete repository scans.

findings.title: Any mention of origin is reported as an origin check
findings.description: A browser-message receiver is classified as origin-checked when its captured statement merely contains the text origin. Logging event.origin, copying it, comparing it without rejecting, or using an unrelated identifier such as original is therefore treated as authorization. This can prevent the missing-authorization check from describing the actual weakness accurately.
findings.recommendation: Require a recognized comparison of event.origin against a fixed or configured allowlist together with a rejecting control-flow branch. Otherwise retain authorization as unknown; use none only when absence is established confidently.

findings.title: Recursive enumeration can follow directory links outside the repository
findings.description: ResolveTarget performs lexical containment only, and recursive enumeration pushes every non-ignored child directory without rejecting symbolic links, junctions, or other reparse points. A repository-controlled link can cause the sensor to read files outside the repository and emit paths containing parent traversal segments, potentially exposing unrelated source or configuration in persisted evidence.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate each traversed directory against the canonical repository root, skip reparse points by default, and maintain a visited-directory identity set to prevent cycles. Record skipped links as diagnostics when they affect completeness.

findings.title: Expression-bodied controller actions can be assigned another method's body
findings.description: The controller analyzer searches for the next opening brace anywhere after an action signature and only verifies that it is inside the controller. For an expression-bodied or abstract action, that brace may belong to a later action or nested construct. Side effects and response behavior from the unrelated block are then attributed to the wrong endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Parse controller members with Roslyn, or at minimum detect an expression-body token and stop at that member's terminating semicolon while bounding brace searches before the next member declaration.
